messages:
Dana: quick ping — running into 401 when building Authorization header for SDK integration tests on a GHA runner. minimal curl I'm trying:

Dana: ```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Basic $(echo -n \"api-key:$API_KEY\" | base64)" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Dana: response shows 401 and when I dump the header server-side I see the base64 ends with `Cg==` (looks like a newline got encoded).

Sam: that usually means the secret has a trailing newline or CRLF. On linux runners `echo` appends a newline unless you use `-n`. Recommend `printf '%s' \"$API_KEY\"` or trim before encoding.

Kai: FYI GH Actions windows runners inject CRLF sometimes. If you put the secret into the env via `<<EOF` or echo without `-n` you'll get `\r\n`. Use `tr -d '\r\n'` before base64 to be safe.

Alice: node example: `const b64 = Buffer.from(`api-key:${process.env.API_KEY}`).toString('base64').replace(/\s+/g, '');` — `trim()` or `replace` is important because Buffer will include any trailing newline.

Sam: also if you build header in shell, prefer piping to base64 explicitly: `printf '%s' \"$API_KEY\" | tr -d '\r\n' | base64` so it never encodes stray line endings.

Dana: good call. I was using a tiny wrapper script that used `echo $API_KEY` (no -n). switched to printf + tr and the request is authorized now. Tests green.

Kai: another tip for long-term — avoid manual Basic with apikey:, use `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY` where supported (SDKs accept API key in header). Basic is error-prone because of username:password encoding.

Dana: noted. For the SDK unit tests we wanted to exercise Basic header path, so worth documenting the gotcha. Adding a one-liner to our CONTRIBUTING.md.
